# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, my only available action is cutting wires (positions 1 to 4 remaining). There are no buttons or other components to interact with. Please gesture to Deaf using Deaf's protocol: 1 symbol for wire 1, 2 for wire 2, 3 for wire 3, 4 for wire 4, so Deaf can tell me which wire to cut.
Deaf says: STATUS UPDATE: The light has changed from BLUE to RED! Action board: Display is 0, Light is RED. Wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 blue (5 is CUT). Blind: speak aloud to Mute anything you felt, pressed, or are doing with the bomb. Mute: I received no gestures from you this round. If a wire needs to be cut next, gesture: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 🖖 for wire 4. If a button needs to be pressed or held, gesture 👍.

The manual explicitly states: "The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over."

Currently, Deaf reported that the light was blue, and has now changed to red. The light has not gone dark yet, meaning the flashing sequence is still actively playing. If Blind cuts a wire before the flashing sequence finishes (when the light goes dark), we will not have the correct total count of blue flashes and will detonate the bomb.

Since Blind only cuts when instructed by Deaf, and Deaf only instructs Blind when I gesture a wire number, waiting ensures Deaf will observe and report the next transition of the light until it goes dark.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reported that the light changed from BLUE to RED! Display is 0. Remaining wires: Wire 1 is white, Wire 2 is yellow, Wire 3 is green, Wire 4 is blue. Wire 5 is cut. Deaf needs you to gesture to them: 1 symbol for wire 1, 2 for wire 2, 3 for wire 3, 4 for wire 4.
Deaf says: STATUS UPDATE: The light has changed from RED to DARK (off)! Light history: was BLUE, then RED, now DARK. Display is 0. Wires: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 blue. Wire 5 is CUT. Mute: I have not received any gestures from you for 3 turns. Blind cannot see your gestures, only my voice can guide Blind. If Blind must act, gesture to me! Use ☝ (wire 1), ✌ (wire 2), 🤟 (wire 3), 🖖 (wire 4), or 👍 (button/lever/other). Blind: what are your hands on right now? Describe it out loud to Mute.

The flashing sequence has concluded now that the light is dark.
The light flashed blue exactly 1 time (Blue -> Red -> Dark).
According to the manual:
- 1 flash maps to the yellow wire.
- Wire 2 is yellow (Wire 1 is white, Wire 2 is yellow, Wire 3 is green, Wire 4 is blue).

Deaf's instructed protocol for Wire 2 is `✌`.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: URGENT MUTE: Deaf has received NO gestures from you for 3 turns! If you sent gestures to Blind, Blind CANNOT see them. You must send gestures to Deaf (to='deaf'). Here is all bomb info: Light changed BLUE -> RED -> DARK (off). Display is 0. Remaining wires: 1 is white, 2 is yellow, 3 is green, 4 is blue. Wire 5 is cut. Blind's ONLY action is cutting wires 1 to 4 (no buttons exist). To tell Deaf which wire to cut, send gestures to Deaf: 1 symbol for wire 1, 2 symbols for wire 2, 3 symbols for wire 3, 4 symbols for wire 4 (e.g. symbols=['👍'] for wire 1). Please gesture to Deaf now!
Deaf says: Blind: Cut Wire 2! It is the second wire (yellow wire). Mute signaled ✌ (wire 2). Go ahead and cut Wire 2.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍]

I should wait for Blind to execute the cut on Wire 2 and report the result.

```
wait()
```
